chunks: Al-Tawhid: Hamza al-Alawi, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic:

"There is no private conversation of three except that He is the fourth of them, nor of five except that He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them wherever they are."

He said: He is One, Unique in Essence, distinct from His creation, and with that He described Himself. He encompasses all things through supervision, encompassing, and power. Nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of a particle in the heavens or in the earth, nor smaller than that or larger, in terms of encompassing and knowledge, not by Essence, because locations are defined, contained by four boundaries; so if it were by Essence, it would necessarily imply containment.
ai.seo_question: How is God's presence with creation understood if He is not physically contained within space?
ai.summary: Hamza al-Alawi narrates from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the nature of God's presence in Quran 58:7, distinguishing between essential containment and attribute-based encompassing. The Imam argues that since physical locations are bounded by four limits, God cannot be 'with' creation by His Essence (Dhat), but rather by His Knowledge, Power, and Supervision (Sifat). This aligns with the Shia theological principle of God's transcendence (Tanzih) from spatial dimensions while maintaining His omnipresence through attributes.
